## Dangerous fire weather is already more likely than a century ago


::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![The chance of fire weather as extreme as Black Summer (2019–20) is already higher than in the early 1900s, and could become about eight times higher if the world warms by 2°C. Filled dots show the best estimate and open circles show the lowest likely value. Real weather records only give a lowest likely value, so the true figure could be higher. Data: van Oldenborgh et al. ## Rising heat is doing most of the work


::: {#tbl-drivers .cell tbl-cap='Heat is the main reason fire weather has become more dangerous, while rainfall shows no long-term climate change trend. The number columns show how important each weather ingredient is as a cause of the rise in fire danger. Data: van Oldenborgh et al. (2021).'}
::: {.cell-output-display}


|Weather ingredient     | How many of the 4 climate models found it as the biggest cause| Its rank in real weather records (1 = biggest cause)|What the study found                                                                                                                                                                          |
|:----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------:|----------------------------------------------------:|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|Heat                   |                                                              3|                                                    1|Explains about half of the rise in fire danger in two models. Hot weeks like December 2019 are now at least 2× as likely, and 1–2°C hotter than in the early 1900s.                           |
|Dry air (low humidity) |                                                              1|                                                    2|The biggest cause in one model, and shares the lead with heat and wind in another.                                                                                                            |
|Rainfall and drought   |                                                              0|                                                    3|No climate change trend in extreme drought, even though 2019 was Australia's driest year on record. More than half of the 2019 dry spell came from natural swings in ocean and wind patterns. |
|Wind                   |                                                              0|                                                    4|Shares the lead with heat and dry air in one model. Otherwise the smallest cause.                                                                                                             |
